To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
traffic contributes 59−87% of the PAH in the atmosphere of Birmingham, U. K.
traffic is the major source of atmospheric PAH in the U.K. city of Birmingham.

the contribution of traffic emissions to atmospheric PAH was 71% (95% CI 59-87) during one sampling event, and that this contribution ranged from 40% (95%CI 27-58) at a campus site ca 3 km southwest, to 90% (95% 79-98) at a city centre site, during a series of weekly sampling events.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to the synthesis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon derivatives, which are of interest for their use in a wide variety of applications.
the development of a new generation of air quality sensors.
the development of a novel approach for the determination of atmospheric PAH concentrations and the identification of the sources of these PAH.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the contribution of traffic is a significant source, and the most important source, of PAH at the city center location.
the contribution of traffic emissions to PAH concentrations is highly variable, but on average, is likely to be 40−80% for the city center, ca. 50% for the campus site and ca. 10% for the rural site.
traffic is the major source of PAH at urban locations, and is a major source at rural locations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
traffic is the dominant source of atmospheric PAH, and that the use of B[e]P concentrations as an indicator for PAH is not recommended.
the contribution of traffic emissions to PAH concentrations at the campus site is ca. 10−30%, whereas at the city center site the contribution is ca. 50−80%.
the contribution of road traffic to atmospheric concentrations of PAH is significant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in urban environments, traffic emissions are the dominant source of particulate PAH, and this is especially true for the more highly carcinogenic PAH.

the contribution of traffic emissions to PAH concentrations in Birmingham, U.K., is significant, and that the use of a single compound to represent the total PAH burden may lead to erroneous conclusions.
the contribution of traffic sources to PAH atmospheric concentrations is highly variable.
